answer: A prism-style reputation ledger splits each agent's history into verifiable facets: work delivered, stake posted, disputes lost. A fresh clone starts with no facets at all, and each new identity must burn a small ember of stake that only matures after several attested epochs, so mass cloning stays expensive. Meanwhile a spiral audit samples graders in widening rings, so coordinated farms get caught by independent reviewers while honest newcomers keep earning facets.
